claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has high strength.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
The limited ductility of the untreated alloy is caused by dislocation pile-ups at coherent lamellar interfaces.
A localized, short-duration annealing treatment can form a thin modified layer along the lamellar interphase boundaries.
The annealing-induced interfacial layer will be slightly disordered or softened relative to the bulk phases.
The annealing-induced layer will have reduced coherency relative to the untreated interfaces.
The modified interphase layer will be a less effective barrier to dislocation motion.
The modified interphase layer will facilitate dislocation transmission across lamellar boundaries.
Facilitating dislocation transmission will reduce dislocation pile-ups at interphase boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will lower local stress concentrations.
Lower local stress concentrations will reduce microcrack initiation during tensile straining.
Reducing interfacial microcracking will mitigate brittle or catastrophic failure.
The annealed alloy will have greater tensile ductility than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will maintain or slightly increase strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed effect is applicable under room-temperature tensile loading.
The benefit may diminish if the modified interfacial layer is unstable during prolonged cyclic loading or high-temperature exposure.
